scope: Policy inputs of the full-loop coverage check in tools/prepare_deep_frontier_map.py (docs/maps.md, Full game loop). Every other requirement is read from the generated blueprints, recipes and narrative settings in src/DeepFrontier/Data and the game's Blueprints.zip. The numbers here are the authored minimums that the data cannot imply.

largeFootprint.why: A building of the Iron Teeth building collection needs a checked flat site when either footprint side is at least this long, or when it is a power generator (WorkshopPoweredGeneratorSpec or GoodPoweredGeneratorSpec). Buildings with a special placement spec always need their special site. Buildings/Platforms pieces are excluded: the player places them on their own structures.

minVeinsWithMineSite.why: Deep Mines are the only permanent deep ore. Two veins with checked mine sites keep the late game alive if one site is lost to flooding or a meltdown.

minDrillSites.why: Two Deep Drill sites next to separate Deep Ore Sources, so the drill phase does not depend on one spot.

finiteDeepOreMargin.why: The drillable Deep Ore Sources of a map (each with a checked Deep Drill site within 25 cells) must hold the DeepOre of one of each collection building (raw material, expanded by the ProgramModel from the generated costs and recipes) plus this share, so a colony can build the whole collection before its Deep Mines run; the launch program and everything after come from the permanent Deep Mines. A source holds at most its StockpileSpec.MaxCapacity (tools/create_vertical_slice_content.mjs).

minUndergroundRuinsReachable.why: Ruin scrap is finite and smaller than one of each building plus three launches (see the program report). The vanilla Efficient Mine on Underground Ruins is the renewable scrap source.

startRoute.why: Route length (cells) from the starting location for the start-game resource counts.

minTreesNearStart.why: Logs, planks and the kiln's log fuel in the first seasons.

minPinesNearStart.why: Pine resin for treated planks (TreatedPlank: Plank + PineResin), which the archive, airframe and payload chains consume.

fieldWaterReach.why: Cells from clean water counted as irrigated farmland.

minFieldCellsNearStart.why: Irrigated, dry, flat, free cells for the first farms.

minShoreBanks.why: Reachable bank cells where the Gatherer Flag's shore fishing (ShoreFishingSpec) can catch the first FreshFish: FishOil (canned fish, bot maintenance) and the hatchery's breeding stock.

shoreRoute.why: Route length (cells) from the start for the reported near-start bank count. A start river shallower than MinimumDepth can be dammed deeper by normal building.

minHydroHead.why: Natural bed drop (layers) of a source-fed river reach that a dam and Reinforced Hydro Turbine can use; the dam adds the rest of the head.

hydroWindow.why: Wet cells walked along the river from the dam site when measuring the natural drop.

launchProgramMissions.why: The DeepOre, scrap and stone report covers every RocketMission recipe once (no failures).

rawGoods.why: Goods the raw-material report does not expand: gathered, grown, pumped, scavenged, map-sourced, or produced as a by-product. Explosives (5 Badwater) is left raw because it is badwater-only; RadioactiveWaste is the by-product of making EnrichedFuel.

recipeChoices.why: The recipe the raw-material report follows for each intermediate good (the main production route of docs/progression.md).

acceptedGaps.why: Loop-coverage items accepted on every map until a design decision. tools/prepare_deep_frontier_map.py prints each one on every run; a map may not declare them as its own unmet items. Empty since 2026-10-30: the last one, finite deep ore covers one of each building, is enforced (finiteDeepOreMargin).
